open_points.subject: A13 owner-session cookie
open_points.text: carried by a cookie that scripts cannot read, sent only over HTTPS when the interface is reached from another machine (R0-29), and only to Registry's own origin
open_points.question: Which exact cookie scope and attributes implement “Registry's own origin,” given that cookies are not scoped by port and the interface may also be reached locally without HTTPS?
options: A host-only HttpOnly cookie with Secure always
A host-only HttpOnly cookie with Secure only for HTTPS deployments
A cookie additionally restricted by a specified path and SameSite policy
open_points.default_guess: Use a host-only, HttpOnly, Secure, SameSite=Strict cookie scoped to the owner-interface path.

open_points.subject: A13 confirmation expiry
open_points.text: It is valid only in that session, while less than 10 minutes have passed since it was shown — an expired one is refused and cleared ... A submission ... giving another value, is refused and leaves the pending value as it was.
open_points.question: When the pending confirmation is expired but the submission gives a different value, is the expired pending confirmation cleared or left in place?
options: Expiry is checked first and clears it
Value equality is checked first and leaves it
Both conditions are reported and it is cleared
open_points.default_guess: Check expiry first and clear the expired confirmation.

open_points.subject: A13 confirmation input binding
open_points.text: kept as a digest of those values in a fixed order ... a submission's inputs are bound when their digest equals it
open_points.question: What exact canonical encoding, field order, digest algorithm, and treatment of absent versus blank values are used to calculate the confirmation binding?
options: A canonical serialization and cryptographic digest declared by the specification
The operation's wire encoding in declared field order
A server-private structured comparison without a digest
open_points.default_guess: Use a versioned canonical serialization in declared field order and SHA-256.

open_points.subject: A13 confirmation consumption
open_points.text: is used up by the first submission that carries it
open_points.question: What atomic ordering guarantees that two concurrent submissions carrying the same pending value cannot both pass the one-time check?
options: Serialize all mutations of one owner session
Atomically compare-and-clear the pending value
Allow both checks but only one domain transaction to commit
open_points.default_guess: Atomically compare-and-clear the pending value before continuing.

open_points.subject: A13 random values
open_points.text: each is compared in constant time
open_points.question: Does constant-time comparison apply only after locating a session, or must lookup of the cookie's session identity itself avoid data-dependent comparison and timing?
options: Only equality checks are constant-time after lookup
Session lookup must also be implemented as a constant-time scan
Store a keyed digest for lookup and constant-time compare the remaining values
open_points.default_guess: Look up a keyed digest of the session identity, then use constant-time equality for submitted secret values.

open_points.subject: A14 no-op audit erasure
open_points.text: An accepted action that changes nothing ... writes no entry, but for the erasure of old audit entries (A15 rule 6).
open_points.question: Is an audit erasure that removes no old entry formally a state-changing action because it appends its own entry, or is it a no-op exception to the requirement that only state-changing actions write entries?
options: It is state-changing because its own entry is new state
It is a no-op exception that nevertheless writes an entry
open_points.default_guess: Treat it as an explicit no-op exception.

open_points.subject: A14 confirmation id for empty erasure
open_points.text: A confirmation id is minted only for an accepted, confirmed action that changes state ... a confirmed action that changes nothing mints none.
open_points.question: Does an accepted audit erasure that removes no entry mint a confirmation id, as A15 rule 6 requires, or mint none under A14 rule 5?
options: Mint the confirmation id required by A15
Mint none because no prior entry was removed
open_points.default_guess: Mint the confirmation id required by A15.

open_points.subject: A15 erasure cutoff time
open_points.text: The date of an erasure is a date not later than today, the current date in UTC
open_points.question: For a request crossing UTC midnight, at what instant is “today” fixed: arrival, confirmation validation, transaction start, or commit?
options: Request arrival
Transaction start
Commit
open_points.default_guess: Fix now and today at transaction start.

open_points.subject: A16 import referential checks
open_points.text: it names a project or room the file does not hold
open_points.question: Which imported record kinds are permitted or required to name a room, and which exact references must be checked, since the stated Room and ArtifactPointer models name projects but no listed imported model names a room?
options: Only room-to-project and pointer-to-project references exist
The migration format contains additional room references that must be declared
The mention of a room is an error and should be removed
open_points.default_guess: Treat the mention of a record naming a room as an error; check only the relationships declared by the models.

open_points.subject: A16 v1 customer grouping
open_points.text: one for each distinct v1 `customer_ref` a picked project names
open_points.question: What equality determines that two v1 customer-reference values are distinct, including whitespace, case, Unicode normalization, and values that are blank?
options: Exact code-point equality with blank meaning no customer
Exact byte equality, including blank as a value
A normalized comparison declared by the import format
open_points.default_guess: Use exact stored-text equality and treat absent or blank as no customer.

open_points.subject: A16 malformed unpicked records
open_points.text: Registry checks what the picks bring in ... and nothing else of the file ... records only of projects the owner did not pick are neither checked ... A file that cannot be read ... or that holds two project records with one id, is refused whole at upload
open_points.question: Besides duplicate project ids and an unreadable envelope, may arbitrary malformed room, pointer, status, instant, or reference data belonging only to unpicked projects remain in an accepted file?
options: Yes, all such unpicked data is ignored
No, structural malformation anywhere refuses the upload
Syntax is checked globally but domain validity is checked only for picked projects
open_points.default_guess: Check global syntax only, and apply domain validation solely to records brought by the picks.

open_points.subject: A16 import concurrency
open_points.text: At confirmation Registry checks again. Any conflict ... refuses the whole import ... An accepted import stores every picked project ... in one transaction.
open_points.question: How is an import ordered against concurrent ordinary creates or writes that could introduce an id conflict after the confirmation check but before the import commits?
options: Serialize the import with every record-creating transaction
Rely on uniqueness constraints so exactly one transaction wins
Permit the ordinary write to fail after the import commits
open_points.default_guess: Use store uniqueness constraints and transaction isolation so one transaction commits and the other is refused cleanly.

open_points.subject: A16 post-import backup
open_points.text: right after it Registry makes a backup run outside the daily schedule
open_points.question: If a checked daily backup already exists for that UTC day, must the post-import run create a second backup, replace the day's backup, or make no backup until the next day?
options: Create an additional post-import backup
Replace the earlier same-day backup
Skip it because the daily maximum was reached
open_points.default_guess: Create an additional post-import backup so the import is protected immediately.

open_points.subject: A17 configuration namespace
open_points.text: A missing, malformed or unknown item fails the start
open_points.question: What exact namespace is Registry's configuration, and which extra host environment variables or configuration-file keys count as unknown items that must stop startup?
options: Only keys in a dedicated Registry configuration object are checked
Every environment variable visible to the process is checked
Unknown keys are ignored
open_points.default_guess: Validate only a dedicated Registry configuration object and reject unknown keys within it.

open_points.subject: A17 secret length
open_points.text: A secret ... is at least 32 bytes long
open_points.question: How is byte length measured for textual configuration values, and are secrets decoded from a required encoding before the length and equality checks?
options: UTF-8 encoded byte length of the literal value
A required base64 decoding to at least 32 raw bytes
A required hexadecimal decoding to at least 32 raw bytes
open_points.default_guess: Require base64-encoded secrets decoding to at least 32 random bytes.

open_points.subject: A17 owner-only startup
open_points.text: one service token for each service ... or, for an owner-only start, none of the four
open_points.question: How does Registry distinguish an intentional owner-only start from an accidentally missing set of all four service tokens?
options: The absence of all four always means owner-only mode
An explicit owner-only mode flag is required
Owner-only mode uses a separate startup command
open_points.default_guess: Require an explicit owner-only startup mode.

open_points.subject: A18 backup frequency after import
open_points.text: Besides the run after an accepted import (A16), which counts as that day's backup, at most one backup is made per UTC day
open_points.question: Does “at most one backup” include the post-import run when an earlier backup already exists that day, or is the post-import run an exception allowed to create a second backup?
options: One total backup per day, so the post-import run is skipped
The post-import run is an exception and may make a second backup
The post-import run replaces the earlier backup
open_points.default_guess: Allow an extra post-import backup.

open_points.subject: A18 backup encryption
open_points.text: Each backup is encrypted with the backup key
open_points.question: Which authenticated-encryption algorithm, nonce generation, file format, key interpretation or derivation, and metadata authentication rules define a valid encrypted backup?
options: A versioned AEAD backup format declared here
Encryption supplied by the store engine
Encryption supplied by the host filesystem only
open_points.default_guess: Use a versioned AEAD format with a fresh random nonce and authenticate all cleartext metadata.

open_points.subject: A18 backup metadata
open_points.text: A backup records, readable without its key, its instant, the release that made it, the last audit sequence number it holds and a digest of the key
open_points.question: Are the cleartext metadata authenticated by the encrypted backup, and what exact key-digest algorithm and domain separation are used?
options: All metadata is authenticated as AEAD associated data
A signed or MACed metadata header is used
Metadata is unauthenticated
open_points.default_guess: Authenticate the metadata as AEAD associated data and use a domain-separated SHA-256 digest for key identification.

open_points.subject: A18 failed temporary-file removal
open_points.text: A removal that fails is reported; the run then makes no backup and counts as failed ... A backup or a deletion that fails leaves no partial file
open_points.question: When removal of an existing temporary or partial file fails, may that file remain, or must Registry somehow guarantee that no partial file remains?
options: The file remains and blocks later runs until removal succeeds
Startup must fail until it can be removed
The file is moved to a quarantine name
open_points.default_guess: Leave it under its temporary name, report failure, and block backup creation until a later cleanup succeeds.

open_points.subject: A18 temporary-file cleanup
open_points.text: at every start and every run Registry first removes every temporary file left there
open_points.question: How does Registry identify its own temporary files so it does not remove unrelated files in the configured backup location?
options: The backup location is required to be Registry-exclusive
Only files matching a release-defined name and authenticated header are removed
Every temporary-looking file in the directory is removed
open_points.default_guess: Require a Registry-exclusive backup directory and a strict release-defined filename prefix.

open_points.subject: A18 run ordering
open_points.text: Every day at the same run ... Registry deletes every backup made more than 30 × 24 hours before
open_points.question: Does retention deletion happen before or after temporary cleanup, creation, verification, and publication of the new backup?
options: Delete old backups before creating the new one
Create and verify the new backup before deleting old ones
Deletion and creation are independently ordered operations
open_points.default_guess: Clean temporary files, delete expired backups, then create and verify the new backup.

open_points.subject: A18 last-run status
open_points.text: The owner interface shows ... whether the last run failed
open_points.question: What counts as a failed run, and where is that status kept so it survives a restart without becoming an undeclared store record or configuration item?
options: Any cleanup, deletion, creation, or verification failure marks the run failed and status is durable
Only backup creation or verification failure counts and status is reconstructed from backup files
The status is runtime-only and is lost on restart
open_points.default_guess: Treat any run-step failure as failure and keep a small durable backup-status record outside the production store.

open_points.subject: A18 checked backup holding the import
open_points.text: the owner interface shows when [the import] has [reached a checked backup]
open_points.question: What exact evidence proves that a checked backup contains the accepted import, especially if its audit entry has been erased: closure presence in the checked copy, sequence comparison, backup instant, or another marker?
options: Open the checked copy and verify that it contains the migration closure and matching digest
Compare the backup's last sequence with the import entry's sequence
Use only the backup instant after the closure instant
open_points.default_guess: During verification, check that the backup copy contains the migration closure with the accepted file digest.

open_points.subject: A01 owner-form request id
open_points.text: The owner interface makes one when it renders a create form
open_points.question: After a refused submission or validation error, does the re-rendered form retain the same request id or mint a new one?
options: Retain it until a create is accepted or the owner abandons the form
Mint a new id on every rendered response
Retain it only for technical failures, not validation refusals
open_points.default_guess: Retain the same request id while redisplaying the same attempted create.

open_points.subject: A01 request-id generation
open_points.text: an opaque value the caller makes, unique for every create it means as new
open_points.question: What format and collision-resistance requirement must owner-interface and Kernel request-id generators meet, since Registry cannot verify that a reused value represents the same intended create?
options: A UUID generated randomly
At least 128 random bits in an opaque string
Any caller value, with collisions handled only as repeats or refusals
open_points.default_guess: Require at least 128 random bits, represented as a UUID.

open_points.subject: A04 check stages
open_points.text: (2) for agent authority, the session and its set ... (6) the record's lifecycle — archived, erased, anonymised, not in the set, a customer's eligibility, a conflict
open_points.question: Is “project not in the session's set” exclusively a stage-2 authorization check, or is it also a stage-6 lifecycle check?
options: Stage 2 only
Stage 6 only
Checked at stage 2 for agent calls and stage 6 for another specified case
open_points.default_guess: Treat it exclusively as stage 2.

open_points.subject: A04 operation time
open_points.text: Every operation ... checks in one order, and the first failure is its answer
open_points.question: Is one value of `now` fixed for all time-dependent checks and recorded instants in an operation, or may each check and write observe a different time?
options: Fix now at transaction start
Fix now at request arrival
Evaluate time separately at every check and write
open_points.default_guess: Fix a single UTC instant at transaction start.

open_points.subject: restored retention-review record
open_points.text: a governance document ... naming each action by its date, kind and the `customer_ref` or `project_id` it touched
open_points.question: How does that record represent an erasure of old audit entries, which touches neither a customer nor a project but must preserve the cutoff date for restoration?
options: Allow an audit-erasure action with no customer or project subject and a cutoff-date field
Use a store-history subject
Record audit erasures in a separate governance section
open_points.default_guess: Allow a subjectless audit-erasure record carrying its cutoff date.

open_points.subject: restored audit cutoff
open_points.text: the latest date audit entries were erased by
open_points.question: Does “latest date” mean the greatest cutoff date ever supplied, or the cutoff supplied by the most recently performed erasure action?
options: Greatest cutoff date
Cutoff from the chronologically latest action
Replay every recorded audit erasure in action order
open_points.default_guess: Use the greatest cutoff date, since smaller later cutoffs cannot restore entries already erased.
